title: The North Face Arcus review: sold for two, best for one
dek: A three-pole DAC Featherlite tent with a pre-bent vestibule pole and a tapered floor. Its detailed owner review calls it a solo tent with elbow room.
subject: The North Face Arcus
verdict: The Arcus pitches quickly with clip-and-hook pole joints and a pre-bent vestibule pole, and its light fly is pleasant in summer sun. But the tapered floor won't fit two pads, the vestibule is small and high, and it's heavy for what it is. Treat it as a roomy solo tent.
bestFor: Solo campers, including tall ones, on summer trips.
notFor: Two people, gear-heavy trips, or weight-conscious backpacking.
pros: Quick, simple pitch with clip-and-hook pole joints

body:
## The short version

The Arcus (listed as the Arcus 23) is a three-pole tent from around 2013 with a coffin-shaped floor that narrows at the foot. Its one detailed owner review on Trailspace sums it up: truly, it's a solo tent, with some elbow room.

## The pole layout

Two long DAC Featherlite poles cross to form the main dome, and a shorter, pre-bent pole arches over the front vestibule. Small clips and wire-gate hooks join the poles where they cross, so each intersection uses one attachment point. Setup is quick and simple.

## Space

One tall, broad-shouldered person fits comfortably. Two people don't, even on 20-inch pads, because the floor tapers. You can sit up in only one spot, facing the foot end, toward a solid wall.

## Vestibule and ventilation

The vestibule is short, sits high off the ground and has one door on the short end, so gear stored there blocks the way in. Ventilation was good with the rear vent and vestibule door open, but with everything sealed overnight, condensation formed under the vestibule. The front vent adjusts only from inside, the rear only from outside.

## Poles and parts

The Arcus uses **3 poles**, **DAC Featherlite aluminum, press-fit**.

Some of these figures come from owner reports rather than the published spec sheet.

The vestibule pole is pre-bent and shorter than the two main poles, so choose the pre-bent option when searching by size for that one.

The North Face doesn't publish pole lengths. To match a replacement, lay your pole out straight, measure tip to tip, count the sections, and read the diameter printed near a joint (or use calipers). Then search the Arcus in our [pole and parts finder](/poles?model=Arcus), compare against measured stock in the [pole size chart](/poles/sizes), or search by measurement in [find a pole by size](/poles/size).

## Bottom line

As a solo summer tent with room to stretch, the Arcus works. As a two-person backpacking tent it falls short, and at 4 pounds 8 ounces it's heavy for one.
